final class RestoreIntegrityServiceTests: XCTestCase {
    func testRejectsDuplicateCard() {
        var state = validStateTemplate()
        guard let duplicateCard = state.waste.last else {
            return XCTFail("Expected at least one waste card in the template.")
        }
        // Discard some other, unrelated card entirely so the total count
        // stays at 52 while introducing a genuine same-id duplicate — the
        // count check alone would otherwise mask the duplicate-detection
        // path being exercised.
        _ = state.stock.removeLast()
        state.stock.append(duplicateCard)

        let result = RestoreIntegrityService().validate(state)
        guard case .invalid(let reason) = result else {
            return XCTFail("Expected duplicate-card board to be invalid.")
        }
        XCTAssertTrue(reason.localizedCaseInsensitiveContains("duplicate"))
    }

    func testRejectsIncompleteDeck() {
        // Note: with Card.id derived purely from suit+rank over a fixed
        // 52-value domain, "52 unique ids" and "all 52 cards present" are
        // logically equivalent — a state can never have exactly 52 unique
        // ids while missing a rank, since the only way to reach 52 again
        // after removing one card is to duplicate another, which the
        // duplicate check (run before the per-suit completeness check)
        // always catches first. So the reachable way to test the
        // completeness requirement is a genuinely short deck, not a
        // same-count substitution.
        var state = validStateTemplate()
        remove(Card(suit: .hearts, rank: .ace), from: &state)

        let result = RestoreIntegrityService().validate(state)
        guard case .invalid(let reason) = result else {
            return XCTFail("Expected a 51-card deck to be invalid.")
        }
        XCTAssertTrue(reason.localizedCaseInsensitiveContains("mismatch"))
    }

    func testRejectsIllegalTableauRun() {
        var state = validStateTemplate()
        let badTop = Card(suit: .clubs, rank: .three, isFaceUp: true)
        let badNext = Card(suit: .diamonds, rank: .five, isFaceUp: true)
        remove(badTop, from: &state)
        remove(badNext, from: &state)
        state.tableau[0] = [badTop, badNext]

        let result = RestoreIntegrityService().validate(state)
        guard case .invalid(let reason) = result else {
            return XCTFail("Expected illegal tableau transition to be invalid.")
        }
        XCTAssertTrue(reason.localizedCaseInsensitiveContains("tableau"))
    }

    func testRejectsNonMonotonicFoundation() {
        var state = validStateTemplate()
        let illegalTop = Card(suit: .spades, rank: .two, isFaceUp: true)
        let illegalBase = Card(suit: .spades, rank: .three, isFaceUp: true)
        remove(illegalTop, from: &state)
        remove(illegalBase, from: &state)
        state.foundations[.spades] = [illegalBase, illegalTop]

        let result = RestoreIntegrityService().validate(state)
        guard case .invalid(let reason) = result else {
            return XCTFail("Expected non-monotonic foundation to be invalid.")
        }
        XCTAssertTrue(reason.localizedCaseInsensitiveContains("foundation"))
    }

    /// Removes every card matching `target`'s suit+rank from wherever it
    /// currently lives (stock/waste/any foundation/any tableau column), so
    /// callers can relocate a card into a deliberately-illegal position
    /// without silently duplicating it (a card only ever needs removing
    /// from whichever single pile actually holds it, but the tests below
    /// shouldn't have to know or assume which one that is).
    private func remove(_ target: Card, from state: inout GameState) {
        let matches: (Card) -> Bool = { $0.suit == target.suit && $0.rank == target.rank }
        state.stock.removeAll(where: matches)
        state.waste.removeAll(where: matches)
        for suit in Suit.allCases {
            state.foundations[suit]?.removeAll(where: matches)
        }
        for index in state.tableau.indices {
            state.tableau[index].removeAll(where: matches)
        }
    }

    private func validStateTemplate() -> GameState {
        let ordered = DeckFactory.orderedCards()
        let foundations: [Suit: [Card]] = Dictionary(uniqueKeysWithValues: Suit.allCases.map { ($0, []) })

        return GameState(
            stock: Array(ordered.dropFirst(7)),
            waste: Array(ordered.prefix(7)),
            foundations: foundations,
            tableau: Array(repeating: [], count: 7),
            drawMode: .drawOne
        )
    }
}

+    }

+        await freezeTimer()
+        await flushPersistence()
+    }
